local M = {}

function M.setup(opts)
    opts = opts or {}
    local mainMod     = opts.mainMod or "ALT"

    local fileManager = opts.fileManager or "nautilus"

    -- Overview / Toggle Viewer (scrolloverview plugin)
    -- Dispatches native overview toggle, with fallback to hyprctl
    hl.bind(mainMod .. " + G", function()
        if hl.plugin and hl.plugin.scrolloverview and hl.plugin.scrolloverview.overview then
            hl.dispatch(hl.plugin.scrolloverview.overview("toggle all"))
        else
            hl.exec_cmd("hyprctl dispatch scrolloverview:overview 'toggle all'")
        end
    end)

    -- Screenshots (hyprshot)
    hl.bind("Print",         hl.dsp.exec_cmd("hyprshot -m region --freeze --clipboard-only --silent"))

    hl.bind(mainMod .. " + SHIFT + V", hl.dsp.exec_cmd("hyprctl keyword monitor eDP-1,preferred,auto,1,transform,2"))

    hl.bind(mainMod .. " + B",      hl.dsp.exec_cmd(browser))
    hl.bind(mainMod .. " + Space",  hl.dsp.exec_cmd(menu))
    hl.bind("SUPER + Space",        hl.dsp.exec_cmd("vicinae toggle"))

    hl.bind(mainMod .. " + SHIFT + Q", hl.dsp.exit())
    hl.bind(mainMod .. " + F",         hl.dsp.window.fullscreen({ action = "toggle" }))

### Why That Happened

1. **The Lambda Runtime Quirk**: When a Lua callback function (`function() ... end`) was registered as the keybind handler, line 18 had:

   hl.plugin.scrolloverview.overview("toggle all")()

   This is also why calling `hyprctl dispatch scrolloverview:overview "toggle all"` directly from the terminal worked without issue—it bypassed the Lua lambda entirely.

2. **Lua Module Caching**: Because Lua caches imported files in `package.loaded`, `hyprctl reload` was reusing the previously loaded `keybinds.lua` module in memory instead of reading fresh edits from disk.
